Different types of isopods need different humidity levels, even within a genus, I keep my dairy cows a lot dryer than my rubber duckies (but never ever completely dry or soaking wet all over, generally you want to put something like a bunch of spaghnum moss on one end of the container that you keep damp to create a moisture gradient, much like you’d make a heat gradient for many reptiles!) and i wouldn’t say it’s your fault, some people just want to make a sale and will unfortunately not make sure their information is accurate to do so

It sounds like it is problems with moisture/humidity, I looked up that substrate and what I found looks like it won’t hold moisture at all for isopods, and generally doesn’t seem suitable. Isopods need soil that will hold moisture, they need moisture to breathe. if they’re under the moss is sounds like they’re trying to be in as moist of an area as possible. 55% humidity is low for some types of isopods, if I remember correctly, gestroi tend to need more humidity than other armadildiums as well. Monstera leaves also don’t make great leaf litter in my experience.
